title: Methotrexate, doxorubicin and cisplatin for osteosarcoma
context_label: High-grade osteosarcoma of an extremity or axial skeleton, excluding craniofacial sites, with all disease sites amenable to complete surgical resection; national eligibility age 40 years or younger
indication_text: High-grade osteosarcoma of an extremity or axial skeleton, excluding craniofacial sites, with all disease sites amenable to complete surgical resection; national eligibility age 40 years or younger
purpose: The three medicines act through different mechanisms against osteosarcoma throughout the body. Surgery removes the visible tumour, and chemotherapy before and after surgery aims to reduce recurrence risk.
schedule_label: Surgery-linked reference course: weeks 1–10, surgery week 11, then weeks 12–29
schedule_summary: The reference plan is not a repeating 21-day cycle. Before surgery, doxorubicin 37.5 mg/m² and cisplatin 60 mg/m² are each given on days 1 and 2 of weeks 1 and 6; methotrexate 12 g/m² is given on day 1 of weeks 4, 5, 9 and 10. Surgery is planned for reference week 11. Afterwards, doxorubicin is given on days 1 and 2 of weeks 12, 17, 22 and 26; cisplatin on days 1 and 2 of weeks 12 and 17; methotrexate on day 1 of weeks 15, 16, 20, 21, 24, 25, 28 and 29. Actual dates depend on surgery, recovery, drug clearance and safety review.
administration_text: Methotrexate is infused over 4 hours after at least 6 hours of prescribed hydration and urine alkalinisation. Folinic acid rescue starts 24 hours after the methotrexate infusion starts, usually every 6 hours initially, and is adjusted to timed levels and kidney function. Cisplatin runs over 4 hours with its own fluid prescription. Doxorubicin may be given by intravenous push or a separately prescribed 48-hour central-line infusion.
monitoring_summary: Use the individual test cards below: each test has its own purpose and timing. Safety tests and tumour-response assessment answer different questions.

agents.name: High-dose methotrexate
agents.mechanism: Blocks folate-dependent production of genetic material
agents.explanation: Methotrexate blocks processes that use folate to make DNA, the genetic material. At this high dose it requires carefully timed folinic acid rescue to protect healthy cells. The kidneys remove methotrexate: slow removal can increase exposure and severe toxicity. Hydration, urine alkalinisation, blood levels and rescue are inseparable parts of treatment.
agents.watch: Report mouth ulcers, severe diarrhoea, reduced urine, dry cough, breathlessness or new neurological symptoms urgently. Do not stop rescue medicine or start other medicines yourself.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Severe mouth or bowel inflammation and ulceration, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea
Kidney injury and delayed clearance; toxicity may require prolonged admission and intensified rescue
Liver injury and liver-test changes; lung inflammation
Uncommon serious brain or nerve effects and severe skin reactions
Fertility and pregnancy harm, rare later cancers and serious interactions with other medicines
visual: Tumour and normal cells are affected
Timed folinic acid protects healthy cells

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Disrupts genetic material and the enzyme that repairs it
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin enters deoxyribonucleic acid, the genetic material called DNA, and interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme needed when cells copy and repair their genes. This damages tumour cells. Normal marrow, mouth and heart cells can also be injured.
agents.watch: Report fever, mouth ulcers, breathlessness, ankle swelling, palpitations or pain at the drip immediately.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth ulcers, appetite changes and diarrhoea
Hair loss, fatigue and skin or nail changes
Heart muscle damage or abnormal rhythm; damage can appear later and relates to lifetime anthracycline exposure
Severe local tissue damage if the drug leaks outside the vein; allergic reactions
Fertility and pregnancy harm; uncommon later blood cancers

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links within and between strands of DNA, the genetic material. These links stop cells copying their instructions normally. Kidney cells, the inner ear and nerves may also be injured, so prescribed fluids and organ checks are essential.
agents.watch: Report reduced urine, persistent vomiting, ringing ears, hearing changes, numbness or weakness before further treatment.
risks: Severe nausea and vomiting; dehydration can worsen kidney injury
Kidney damage and low magnesium, potassium or other electrolytes
Hearing loss or ringing in the ears, sometimes permanent
Numbness, tingling or weakness from nerve damage, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Allergic reactions, infusion-site injury, fertility and pregnancy harm

anatomy: New confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness or seizures needs immediate assessment.
Report ringing ears or reduced hearing promptly. Hearing changes can persist.
Report ulcers, painful swallowing or difficulty eating and drinking early.
New breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, faintness or swelling needs urgent assessment.
Blood tests monitor liver effects; report yellow eyes or dark urine promptly.
Report reduced urine or inability to drink. Kidney damage and electrolyte losses may need extra tests.
Fever, shaking chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding requires immediate oncology advice.
Use prescribed anti-sickness support; report persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea or difficulty drinking.

monitoring_schedule.note: The national regimen, product information and individual clinical plan may require different tests. Your treating team writes the actual dates and reviews results before treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check infection, anaemia and bleeding risk for the selected drug phase.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each treatment, with repeat checks as indicated. Methotrexate and doxorubicin/cisplatin use different source treatment thresholds.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney function and daily creatinine
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess high-dose methotrexate clearance and cisplatin injury.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before each treatment; creatinine daily during methotrexate administration and clearance monitoring. Further testing follows a rise in creatinine or delayed clearance.

monitoring_test_details.label: Methotrexate blood concentration
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Guide safe continuation and adjustment of folinic acid rescue.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At 24, 48, 72, 96 and 120 hours as appropriate from the actual infusion START; continue later measurements if the specialist clearance plan requires them.

monitoring_test_details.label: Urine acidity
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Reduce methotrexate precipitation in the kidneys.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Confirm urine pH at least 7 before methotrexate, then check every 6 hours during methotrexate and rescue while prescribed alkalinisation continues.

monitoring_test_details.label: Fluid balance and hydration
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Maintain clearance while identifying fluid retention or reduced output.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Begin prescribed prehydration at least 6 hours before methotrexate; record fluid balance every 4 hours during treatment. Cisplatin has a separate pre/post-hydration prescription.

monitoring_test_details.label: Liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect hepatic effects and interpret persistent abnormalities.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before each treatment; repeat after abnormal results or symptoms. The team distinguishes expected transient methotrexate-related changes from persistent injury.

monitoring_test_details.label: Coagulation and urine screening
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify baseline bleeding and urinary abnormalities.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Coagulation tests and urine dipstick for blood, protein and glucose before starting; repeats are directed by findings and the clinical plan.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart function
monitoring_test_details.timing: Heart tracing before starting; imaging when clinically indicated. Symptoms or abnormal pumping measurements trigger a specific reassessment before further doxorubicin. The linked doxorubicin product information additionally recommends baseline pumping-function imaging and repeats after approximately each accumulated 100 mg/m². The specialist team reconciles this with the national source and writes the cardiac monitoring schedule.

monitoring_test_details.label: Hearing and nerve assessment
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify cisplatin injury that may change future doses.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Assess hearing symptoms and sensory nerve damage before each course; audiology when clinically indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Surgery, pathology and tumour review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Connect local treatment, response and postoperative planning.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Plan surgery at reference week 11 after induction, review resection/pathology afterwards, and individualise imaging and follow-up.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm the entire methotrexate admission, rescue, blood-level and interaction plan. Ask oncology/pharmacy before any new prescription, over-the-counter painkiller, antibiotic or supplement. Agree the operation and recovery plan, fertility preservation and line arrangements. Cisplatin has high nausea/vomiting risk; doxorubicin and high-dose methotrexate have moderate risk. Each visit needs its own reconciled anti-sickness prescription. Methotrexate hydration, alkalinisation, level monitoring and folinic acid rescue must continue until the specialist team confirms safe clearance. Delayed clearance may need intensified rescue or glucarpidase. No fixed discharge day is promised. Low blood counts or a delay to the next chemotherapy dose must not automatically withhold or stop folinic acid rescue for methotrexate already given.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Never change pump settings or disconnect an infusion yourself.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Obtain written contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine, including how long precautions continue after the final dose. Different medicines have different requirements. Contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible. Children and young people need age-appropriate information, assent and the applicable parent or guardian consent process.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team plans chemotherapy together with complete removal of the tumour and any other resectable disease sites. The operation, reconstruction, rehabilitation and pathology review are central parts of the plan. Radiotherapy can be considered when surgery is not feasible or margins are inadequate; it is not automatically added to every osteosarcoma course.

evidence.title: EURAMOS-1: preoperative platform and randomised methotrexate, doxorubicin and cisplatin plus ifosfamide and etoposide versus methotrexate, doxorubicin and cisplatin in poor responders
evidence.summary: The international study established a large practical treatment platform. In the separate randomised comparison after a poor pathological response, adding ifosfamide and etoposide did not improve event-free survival and increased toxicity. The specialist team interprets pathology together with the whole treatment plan.

evidence.caveat: The pre-randomisation report is not comparative survival proof. The poor-response randomisation studied postoperative intensification, not treatment of relapse. Its result must not be used to withhold all future salvage options.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: The three medicines act through different mechanisms against osteosarcoma throughout the body. Surgery removes the visible tumour, and chemotherapy before and after surgery aims to reduce recurrence risk. A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team plans chemotherapy together with complete removal of the tumour and any other resectable disease sites. The operation, reconstruction, rehabilitation and pathology review are central parts of the plan. Radiotherapy can be considered when surgery is not feasible or margins are inadequate; it is not automatically added to every osteosarcoma course.

The reference plan is not a repeating 21-day cycle. Before surgery, doxorubicin 37.5 mg/m² and cisplatin 60 mg/m² are each given on days 1 and 2 of weeks 1 and 6; methotrexate 12 g/m² is given on day 1 of weeks 4, 5, 9 and 10. Surgery is planned for reference week 11. Afterwards, doxorubicin is given on days 1 and 2 of weeks 12, 17, 22 and 26; cisplatin on days 1 and 2 of weeks 12 and 17; methotrexate on day 1 of weeks 15, 16, 20, 21, 24, 25, 28 and 29. Actual dates depend on surgery, recovery, drug clearance and safety review.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can treatment restart when a blood test improves?
questions.a: Only when the treating team confirms a new plan. A previous serious reaction, stopped medicine or required protective treatment still matters.

questions.q: How do the operation and other treatments fit?
questions.a: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team plans chemotherapy together with complete removal of the tumour and any other resectable disease sites. The operation, reconstruction, rehabilitation and pathology review are central parts of the plan. Radiotherapy can be considered when surgery is not feasible or margins are inadequate; it is not automatically added to every osteosarcoma course.
